p.seg: Pípóshī Fó
First, Pípóshī Fó,
surname Jūlóu,
of the Kshatriya royal lineage.
Father's name Pánbiǎo,
mother's name Pántóumò,
the country governed was named Chàmòtí.
Gatha says:
The body receives birth from the formless,
like illusions manifesting various images.
The illusory human mind and consciousness are fundamentally empty,
merits and sins are all empty, without anything to dwell upon.
Shīqì Fó
Second, Shīqì Fó,
surname Jūlóu,
of the Kshatriya royal lineage.
Father's name Ālúnná,
mother's name Póluóhē Yuèdī,
the country governed was named Ālóunà Hétí.
Gatha says:
Arising of all good dharmas is fundamentally illusion,
creating all evil karma is also illusion.
The body is like foam, the mind is like wind,
illusions arise without root, without real nature.
Píshèfú Fó
Third, Píshèfú Fó,
His surname was Jūlóu,
of the Kshatriya royal lineage.
His father's name was Xūbōluó Tíhé,
his mother's name was Yéshě Yuè Tí,
and the name of the country he ruled was Ānòu Yōu Mó.
His verse says:
"The four great elements are borrowed to form the body;
The mind is originally without birth, arising due to circumstances.
If the preceding circumstance is absent, the mind is also absent;
Sin and merit are like illusions, arising and ceasing."
Jūliúsūn Buddha
Fourth, Kūrunda Buddha,
his surname was Jiāyè,
of the Brahmin lineage.
His father's name was Āzhīdádōu,
his mother's name was Suíshèjiā,
and the name of the country he ruled was Lúnhēlìtí.
His verse says:
"Seeing the body as unreal is seeing the Buddha;
Understanding the mind as illusory is understanding the Buddha.
Understanding that the nature of body and mind is fundamentally empty,
What difference is there between such a person and the Buddha?"
Jūnágáhmóuní Buddha
Fifth, Kanakamuni Buddha,
his surname was Jiāyè,
of the Brahmin lineage.
His father's name was Yéshǎn Bōduō,
his mother's name was Yù Tuōluó,
The name of the country he governed was Chā Mó Yuè Tí.
The verse says:
To know the Buddha does not see the physical body is to know the Buddha,
If there truly is knowledge, there is no other Buddha.
The wise can know the empty nature of sin,
And be fearless of life and death.
Kāshyapa Buddha
Sixth, Kāshyapa Buddha,
Surname Kāshyapa,
Of the Brahman caste.
His father's name was Ā Jì Dá Yé Pó,
His mother's name was Tán Míng Yuè Tí Yé,
The name of the country he governed was Bō Luó Sī.
The verse says:
The nature of all sentient beings is pure,
From the beginning, there is no birth and nothing to extinguish.
This body and mind are illusory creations,
Within illusion, there is no sin or blessing.
Śākyamuni Buddha
Seventh, Śākyamuni Buddha,
Surname Śākya,
Of the Kshatriya king caste.
His father's name was Yuè Tóu Tán,
His mother's name was Mó Hē Mó Yé,
The name of the country he governed was Jiā Wéi Luó Wèi.
The verse says:
Illusion has no cause and no birth,
All see it as naturally as it is.
All dharmas are nothing but self-transformation,
illusory transformations that are unborn and without fear.
This Śhìjiāmóu​ní​ Fó (釋迦牟尼佛),
is the fourth Buddha within this Bhadrakalpa.
Within the three kalpas,
in the first thousand Buddhas,
Huāguāng Fó (花光佛) is the leader,
down to the Píshèfú Fó (毗舍浮佛),
who attained Buddhahood in the past *zhuāngyánjié* (莊嚴劫);
in the middle thousand Buddhas,
Jūlóusūn Fó (拘樓孫佛) is the leader,
down to the Lóuzhì Rúlái (樓至如來),
who successively attain Buddhahood in the current *xiánjié* (賢劫);
in the latter thousand Buddhas,
Rìguāng Rúlái (日光如來) is the leader,
down to Xūmíxiāng Fó (須彌相佛),
who will attain Buddhahood in the future *xīngxiùjié* (星宿劫).
At the beginning of the *xiánjié* (賢劫),
fragrant water permeated everywhere,
and there were a thousand large lotus
kings. Those in the Fourth Dhyana
saw this auspicious sign,
and said to each other:
"If this world is formed now,
there will be a thousand worthy people appearing in the world."
Therefore,
this time is named *xiánjié* (賢劫).
According to the *Yīngguǒ Jīng* (因果經):
When Shìjiā Rúlái had not yet become a Buddha,
he was a great Bodhisattva,
named Shàn Huì,
also named Rěnrǔ.
His meritorious deeds and practices were complete,
his position ascended to the stage of becoming a Buddha in the next life,
he was born in the Tuṣita Heaven,
named Shèng Shàn,
also called Hù Míng,
and for the various heavenly kings, he expounded on the practices of becoming a Buddha in the next life,
and also manifested himself in the ten directions to preach the Dharma.
When the appointed time was approaching,
he was about to descend to become a Buddha.
He surveyed the various countries to see which was in the center,
and then he knew that the country of Kapilavastu was the most central place on earth.
Therefore, the *Běn Qǐ Jīng* says:
"The Buddha's majestic power,
is supremely honored and revered,
and does not appear in the sloping edges of borderlands."
This city of Kapilavastu
is the center of the three thousand suns and moons, the universe.
The Buddhas of ancient times
all arose here.
The *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* says:
"[It is] in the middle of Jambudvīpa."
The *Shānhǎi Jīng* says:
"The country of Shendu,
Xuānyuán Shì resides there."
Guō Pú 注曰：
That is Central India.
That land divides itself into the Five Indies,
the Central India is the center of heaven and earth,
its name is not "border,"
the meaning of "center" is thus revealed.
The "Karma Sutra" says:
The Central India, Great Xia, has four castes:
namely the Kshatriya (chàlìdì) caste, the Brahmin (póluómén) caste,
the Vaishya (píshèluó) caste, and the Shudra (shǒutuó) caste.
The Kshatriya (chàlì) royal caste is the most noble,
since the beginning of the kalpa,
it has been passed down without interruption;
the remaining three castes
are not what we are discussing here,
but we are only clarifying the Buddha's caste,
which has five different divisions.
Furthermore, the "Long Āgama Sutra" says:
At the beginning of the kalpa,
there were no sun or moon, the radiant
gods, their merit exhausted, descended and were born,
all transformed into humans,
joyfully taking [pleasure] as food,
their body light shone far,
they flew freely,
there was no male or female, noble or base, relatives,
but natural earth flavor,
its taste like clarified butter and honey.
Yǒu shì cháng zhě,
they then began to eat in clumps.
Their light and power completely disappeared,
they cried out in sorrow on the ground.
Eating much made them look withered,
eating little made their forms glossy.
Then arose victory and defeat,
and the taste of the earth disappeared.
Then grew earth skin (a kind of edible fungus),
because they ate the earth skin, therefore
all evils gathered together.
Then grew forest vines and *jīng* rice etc.,
all tastes were sweet and delicious.
Because of eating these, they had male and female organs,
and in this way, developing further,
they became married,
and then began to be born from the womb.
The *Lóu Tàn Jīng* says:
naturally growing *jīng* rice,
harvested in the morning, ripened in the evening.
The *Zhōng Āhán Jīng* says:
the rice was four inches long,
people competed to take it in advance,
and in this way killed each other.
Where they took it in advance,
it did not grow again afterwards.
The *Cháng Āhán Jīng* says:
at that time, the sentient beings having seen that it would not grow again,
Therefore, everyone harbored anxieties and distress,
mutually enclosing fields and residences
to establish boundaries.
From the time people started hoarding for themselves,
stealing others' fields and grain,
disputes arose from this,
and no one could resolve them.
They discussed establishing one person,
called the "Equal Lord,"
to reward good and punish evil,
and they would all provide for him.
At that time, there was a person
of magnificent appearance and stature,
whose imposing presence awed all things.
Trusted and admired by all,
they went and invited him.
Once he accepted,
he then had the name "ruler of the people."
The *Lóutàn Jīng* (《樓炭經》) says:
"The people discussed
making a leader,
and honored him with the title 'King',
collecting taxes according to law,
hence the name *chàlì* (剎利),"
This translates to "lord of fields and land."
At that time, the *Yánfú Tí* (閻浮提) world was prosperous, joyful, peaceful, and secure.
Green grass grew on the ground,
like peacock feathers.
In eighty thousand commanderies and kingdoms, settlements could hear each other,
and there were none suffering from cold, heat, or illness.
The king governed the world with righteous Dharma,
upheld the ten virtues,
and revered each other
like father and son.
People lived extremely long lives,
immeasurable.
Later, there were subsequent kings
who did not practice righteous Dharma,
and their lifespan gradually decreased to ten thousand years.
It diminished gradually like this until now, to a hundred years.
First, at the beginning of the kalpa,
they began to be kings,
passing down from one to another.
To Bodhisattva Shēn Luóluó,
the direct line ended.
Branches of the remaining clan still inherit the throne today,
hence a broad list is provided below, showing the succession of Chakravartins and petty kings.
Initially, the democratic king was named Dàrén,
the second was Zhēnbǎo Wáng,
and then the thirty-third was Shànsī Wáng.
The above thirty-three kings succeeded each other,
and were merely petty kings.
Next, they are all Chakravartin kings,
succeeding each other directly,
until the Bodhisattva.
The *Lóutàn Jīng* says:
Zhēnshé Wáng (真闍王) had a prince,
named Bōzéjiā (波迮迦),
which translates to Great Fish King.
The *Fó Běnxíng Jīng* (佛本行經) says:
In Central India, there is a city,
named Bāoduōnà (褒多那),
where the people are numerous and thriving.
Among them was an emperor
named Great Fish King.
From this king up to the king named Great Renown,
there were descendants succeeding one another.
Counting the descendants, there were eighty-four thousand two hundred and seventy-two kings,
all of whom were Cakravartin kings.
Finally, there were two kings
who were masters of Jambudvipa,
named Máo Cǎo Wáng (茆草王).
Cǎo Wáng (草王) had a prince,
named Great Máo Cǎo Wáng (大茆草王).
Great Máo Cǎo Wáng (大茆草王) had no son to be king,
and he thought:
"My ancestors generation after generation succeeded one another,
all being descendants of Cakravartin kings.
Now I have no heir,
and I fear the lineage will be cut off.
If I renounce the world,
I fear I will sever the royal line;
if I do not renounce the world,
then I will sever the holy line."
After contemplating this,
the king entrusted the affairs of state to his various ministers.
The king then entered the mountains to cultivate the Way,
achieving the five supernatural powers of an immortal,
and was named Wáng Xiān (王仙, King Immortal).
This Wáng Xiān (王仙, King Immortal) previously had a consort
named Shàn Xí (善襲),
who was pregnant in the palace.
Later, she gave birth to a son,
who was a descendant of the Great Máocǎo King (大茆草王).
Later, the various ministers learned that he was the crown prince of King Immortal,
and then solemnly enthroned and consecrated him,
succeeding to the throne.
He was known as Zhē Wáng (遮王, Covering King),
also called Yù Mó Wáng (欝摩王, Luxuriant Rub King),
and also known as Yì Mó Wáng (懿摩王, Beautiful Rub King).
The king had two consorts:
one named Shàn Xián (善賢),
and the other named Miào Duānzhèng (妙端正).
Miào Duānzhèng (妙端正),
gave birth to four princes:
one named Jù Miàn (炬面, Torch Face),
the second named Jīnsè (金色, Golden Color),
the third named Xiàng Zhòng (象眾, Elephant Multitude),
and the fourth named Bié Chéng (別成, Separate Completion).
Consort Shàn Xián (善賢) only gave birth to one son,
named Chángshòu (長壽, Long Life),
who was handsome and pleasing,
The world has few peers,
but he lacks the bone structure
to be worthy of inheriting the throne.
Shànxián thought:
"Wonderful and upright are the four sons,
Jùmiàn and his like,
brothers and kin,
I now have only this one son.
Although he is handsome and upright,
he is unworthy of being king.
What means can I employ
to enable this son of mine to inherit the throne?"
At that time,
the king of Zhē was driving his chariot to the palace gardens,
comforting his concubines.
Shànxián came out
and said to the king:
"I am secure in all things,
but I have one wish
that I intend to ask of the king.
May the king grant it to me."
The king said:
"Whatever your heart desires,
I shall grant it."
Shànxián said:
"The king must not change his mind and regret it;
I beseech the king to swear an oath."
The king said:
"If anyone changes their mind and regrets this,
I, Zhèn, shall be torn into seven pieces."
Shànxián said to the Great King,
"Jùmiàn and the other four sons
should be banished."
The King said,
"These four sons have committed no fault,
why should they be banished?"
The King pondered for a long time.
Because he had made a vow himself, and he did not want to break his promise,
he then decreed that the four sons be banished to another place.
At that time, the four princes said to their father, the King,
"We four have not committed any other transgressions,
yet suddenly we are banished from the country.
Why is this?"
The King said,
"I know that you four sons are indeed without fault,
innocent, and have undeservedly suffered as described above.
This is not my intention,
but the intention of Shànxián."
At that time, the concubines who bore the four boys, along with their relatives, having heard of this matter,
quickly went to the King's location,
and said to the Great King,
"We four sons are being banished by the King's order,
we wish to follow them."
The King said,
"It is appropriate to allow this."
The King then issued an edict,
Continuing to advise his four sons:
"If you wish to marry,
do not marry outside our clan,
it is proper to marry within the inner circle of our surname,
lest the lineage be broken."
These four young men respectfully received the king's instructions,
and then led their families and departed northwards.
They arrived at the Shěyí Grove,
where the land and water were spacious and flat,
without any pits or mounds.
They took their families to live in this grove,
and because their virtue and fortune were abundant,
they eventually formed a great nation.
Later, Zhē Wáng thought and asked his ministers:
"Where are my four sons whom I banished in the past,
where are they now?"
A minister replied:
"Now they are north of the Xiāng Shān,
south of the Xuě Shān,
in between the two mountains, there is a grove
called Shěyí,
the land is fertile and abundant,
the people are thriving,
the common people are flocking to them,
like a market town,
forming a great nation,
and they have established a king,
naming it Ní Jū Luó city.
The place where the ancient immortal Jiāpíluó (迦毗羅) attained enlightenment,
is why the city was established and named."
At that time, Zhē Wáng (遮王) heard this,
and sighed repeatedly,
"My son Shìjiā (釋迦)! My son Shìjiā (釋迦)!"
Therefore, from his virtue was the surname established,
the surname Shìjiā (釋迦).
Shìjiā (釋迦),
translated means "capable benevolence."
Dà Zhē Wáng's (大遮王) three sons had already died,
leaving only Biéchéng (別成),
who was called Ní Jūluó Wáng (尼拘羅王),
he was the Buddha's great-great-grandfather.
This king had a crown prince,
named Jū Lúluó Wáng (拘盧羅王),
he was the Buddha's great-grandfather.
This king had a crown prince,
named Qú Jūluó Wáng (瞿拘盧王),
he was the Buddha's grandfather.
This king had a crown prince,
named Shī Zǐjiá Wáng (師子頰王),
he was the Buddha's father.
This king had four crown princes:
the first was named Shū Tóu Tánnà (輸頭檀那),
that is, Jìngfàn Wáng (淨飯王);
the second was named Shū Jūlú Tánnà (輸拘盧檀那),
that is, Bái Fàn Wáng (白飯王);
the third was named Túlú Nà (途盧那),
Then there was King Húfàn;
the fourth was named Āmítū Tánnà,
then King Gānlùfàn.
King Jìngfàn had two crown princes:
one was named Xīddáduō,
who is the Buddha,
born on the eighth day of the fourth month,
with a height of one zhàng six chǐ;
the second was named Nánduó,
who is the one who sweeps against the wind,
born on the ninth day of the fourth month,
with a height of one zhàng five chǐ four cùn.
King Báifàn had two crown princes:
one was named Tiáodá,
who is the Buddha's cousin,
born on the seventh day of the fourth month,
with a height of one zhàng five chǐ four cùn;
the second was named Ānán,
who is the Buddha's attendant,
born on the tenth day of the fourth month,
with a height of one zhàng five chǐ three cùn.
King Húfàn had two crown princes:
one was named Shì Mónán,
the one who turns soil into gold,
born on the twelfth day of the fourth month,
with a height of one zhàng four cùn.
King Gānlùfàn had two crown princes:
one was named Bō Tóu,
Having renounced the household life,
born on the thirteenth day of the fourth month,
with a height of one *zhang* and four *cun*;
also named Bàtízi,
entered the Way,
born on the fourteenth day of the fourth month,
with a height of one *zhang* and four *cun*.
The *Fó Běnxíng Jīng* says:
At that time,
the Bodhisattva Hùmíng was in the Tuṣita Heaven,
thinking of transforming all sentient beings,
and then instructed the Jīn Tuán Heavenly Being:
"You should carefully observe the lineages of all kings,
and then select a place for my next life."
The Jīn Tuán Heavenly Being received the Bodhisattva's command and observed accordingly.
Having finished observing,
he said to the Bodhisattva:
"There is a Kshatriya lineage,
with the surname Jùtán,
the empress of a Kshatriya,
studies the Way under the great sage Jùtán,
and takes the surname Jùtán from the teacher.
From the beginning,
generation after generation they have been the lineage of the Golden Wheel Kings,
even from the descendants of King Zhē,
descendants succeeding each other,
residing in that Kapilavastu city,
the capital of the Śākya clan.
Among them was a king,
named Shīzǐ Jiá Wáng (師子頰王),
this king had a crown prince
named Shūtóu Tánnà Wáng (輸頭檀那王).
This king now
has a great reputation among all the gods and humans in the world,
and is worthy of being a place for a Bodhisattva to be reborn."
The Bodhisattva exclaimed:
"Excellent! Excellent!
You have observed the lineages of kings well.
As you have said,
I will surely be born there."
The sutra also says:
When the Hùmíng Púsà (護明菩薩) wished to descend,
Māyé Fūrén (摩耶夫人) told Jìngfàn Wáng (淨飯王):
"Great King, you should know,
I now wish to observe the eight precepts of pure fasting."
After the fasting,
she then fell asleep,
and in a dream saw a six-tusked white elephant,
its head vermillion,
its seven limbs supporting the ground,
its tusks adorned with gold,
a heavenly being riding it,
descending from the sky,
heading towards the palace of Jìngfàn Wáng (淨飯王).
According to the Āhán Jīng (阿含經),
regarding the Bodhisattva entering the womb of his mother,

Then, in the twenty-third year of King Zhāo of Zhōu (昭王) the fifth emperor of the Jī Zhōu (姬周) dynasty in this land, in the year guǐchǒu (癸丑), on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, he was entrusted to Māyā (摩耶).
Until the twenty-fourth year, the year jiǎyín (甲寅),
Lady Māyā (摩耶) was playing happily in the Biluó (毗羅) garden,
and saw that the bōluó (波羅) tree blossoms were lovely.
She raised her right hand to grasp a branch,
and the Bodhisattva was born from her right flank,
his body was truly golden,
and his features were perfect.
Also, the *Pǔyào Jīng* (普曜經) says:
When the Buddha was first born, he emitted great light,
illuminating the ten directions,
golden lotuses sprang from the earth,
naturally supporting his feet.
To the east, west, south, and north,
he took seven steps in each direction,
observing the four quarters.
One finger pointing to the sky,
one finger pointing to the earth,
he roared like a lion:
"Above the heavens and below the heavens, I alone am the honored one!"
Furthermore, the gatha (偈) says:
My birth and division of the womb is finished,
this is my last and final body.
I have already attained liberation,
and shall liberate all beings.
After speaking this gatha (偈),
it induced nine dragons to spout water
Bathing the crown prince,
the crown prince having been bathed,
silently, without speaking,
returning to being like a worldly infant.
Furthermore, according to the "Strange Records of the Zhou Dynasty":
In the twenty-fourth year of King Zhāo's reign, the year of jiǎyín
on the eighth day of the fourth month,
rivers, streams, springs, and ponds suddenly overflowed,
palaces, dwellings, mountains, rivers, and the earth all shook completely,
its light had five colors,
penetrating into the main hall,
spreading in all directions.
King Zhāo asked the grand historian Sū Yóu, saying:
"What is this auspicious sign?"
Sū Yóu replied, saying:
"A great sage has been born in the West."
He further asked:
"How will this affect the world?"
Yóu said:
"At this time, there will be nothing,
but a thousand years from now, his teachings will spread to this land,
that is the Buddha. He was first born in King Jìngfàn's palace in the city of Jiāpíluó in the western country of Tiānzhú (India), a response to the auspicious signs in this land."
According to the "Sutra of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination":
When the crown prince reached the age of nineteen,
he grew weary of the palace of empresses,
the father king, fearing he would leave home (become a monk),
then ordered the playing of flutes and music to entertain the crown prince.
The crown prince was not pleased,
Sitting until the third watch,
all five hundred palace women were asleep.
The Pure Abode Heaven deity, being in the empty sky at that time,
spoke a verse to the Crown Prince, saying:
"The world is impure, and the masses are deluded,
nothing surpasses the nature of a woman's body.
Because the world adorns itself with clothing,
foolishness is the source of arising greed.
If a person can make such an observation,
that it is like a dream, like an illusion, not real.
Quickly abandon ignorance, do not be negligent,
and the mind will attain liberation, a body of merit."
Furthermore, a heavenly being, with hands clasped in a window, said to the Crown Prince:
"It is time to leave!"
The Crown Prince, hearing this verse,
felt joy arise in his heart.
He secretly ordered Chē Nì to saddle Jiānzhì and bring him forth.
Four deities held up his feet,
and he went out of the city to the northwest.
The Crown Prince thought:
"Those who renounce the world should have great compassion,
and not leave any horse tracks,
for the king will surely blame the guards."
So, in the northwest corner of the city, he left one horse track
to inform them, and flew away to the northwest.
The time was the forty-second year, rénshēn year, of King Zhōu Zhāo of this land, the eighth day of the second month, at midnight.
According to the 《Lǜ》, it says:
Tàizǐ (太子) having departed,
arrived at Bānchá (斑茶) Mountain in the kingdom of Mójié Tuó (摩竭陀),
and on a rock there, sat in the lotus position.
He made this thought:
"With what should I shave my hair?"
As soon as this thought arose,
a Jingjū Tiānzǐ (淨居天子), the deva of the Pure Abodes, immediately presented a knife.
Tàizǐ (太子) himself took it,
and having shaved his hair,
the Jingjū Tiānzǐ (淨居天子) further presented a simple *saṃghāṭī* robe.
He then took off the clothes he was wearing that day,
and took off his headdress, and the white horse, etc., and entrusted them to Chēnì (車匿)
to take back to the royal palace,
and said a *gāthā* to inform his father, saying:
Even if affection and love last a long time,
when the time comes, life will end and we will part.
Seeing this impermanence in an instant,
therefore, I now seek liberation.
At that time, Tàizǐ (太子) was in the mountains, valiant and diligent,
cultivating the unsurpassed path.
He also went to Ālán Jiālán's (阿藍迦藍) place
for three years, learning the Meditation of the Realm of No-thingness,
knowing it was not the way, he abandoned it.

"Mahākāśyapa (摩訶迦葉) is maintaining his body with samādhi,
Waiting for Mílè (彌勒) to descend and be born,
to hand over the Saṃghāṭī robe completely,
then enter Nirvāṇa.
For now, you absolutely must not cremate him."
The king heard these words,
and with various offerings,
his heart filled with sorrow and longing.
Then he bowed and took leave of the fixed body,
and ordered Ānán (阿難) to enter Rājagṛha.
As King Ajātaśatru (Ājiāshè Wáng 阿闍世王) and Ānán (阿難) just exited this mountain,
the mountain closed up as before.
When the master entered extinction, it
was in the 5th year, Bǐngchén (丙辰), of King Xiào (孝王), the eighth ruler of the Zhōu (周) dynasty in this land.
Chan Master Jìngxīu (淨修禪師) praised, saying:
"How great is Kāśyapa (Jiāyè 迦葉)!
Secretly transmitting the Buddha's mind.
One robe on his body,
his words like a vast ocean.
Dignified and orderly in his conduct,
guiding and transforming profoundly.
Not yet meeting Maitreya (Císhì 慈氏),
he remains fixed on Mount Kukkuta (Jīcén 雞岑)."
Ānán (阿難)
The Second Patriarch, Venerable Ānán (阿難尊者),
was from Rājagṛha (Wángshèchéng 王舍城),
of the Kshatriya (Chàlìdì 剎利帝) clan.
A son of the White Rice King (Báifàn Wángzǐ 白飯王子),
He is the Buddha's younger brother.
Originally, he was the venerable Jīnlóng Buddha,
now transformed by the Tathāgata,
establishing the Dharma banner,
saving sixty thousand people,
raising high the sun of the Buddha,
greatly illuminating the deluded,
being broadly accomplished in total retention (dhāraṇī),
and being foremost in learning.
The master was traveling, and went to a secluded bamboo grove,
and heard a bhikṣu incorrectly reciting a Buddhist verse, saying:
"If a man lives to be a hundred years old,
and does not see the drying up of floods,
it is better to live for one day,
and be able to witness it."
Ānándà, having heard this,
sighed and said:
"The common man in the world,
does not understand the intention of the Buddhas,
vainly carries the four Vedas,
it is better to sleep empty-bodied."
Ānándà, having sighed,
said to the bhikṣu:
"This is not the Buddha's teaching,
now you should listen to me expound the Buddha's verse
which says:
'If a man lives to be a hundred years old,
Being unable to perceive the subtle mechanisms of all Buddhas is not as good as living even a single day and gaining decisive understanding of them (as fully described in the *Bǎolín Zhuàn*)."
and being able to decisively understand it
At that time, Ānán spoke to Shāngnàhéxiū, saying:
"The Tathāgata's Dharma-eye is entrusted to me,
and I now entrust it to you.
You should propagate my teachings,
and not allow them to be cut off."
He further said to Mòtiándǐ:
"The Buddha foretold of you:
'After my Parinirvana,
in the kingdom of Jìbīn, one hundred and twenty years hence, there will be a Bhikshu
named Mòtiándǐ
who will spread the Buddha's Dharma.'"
At that time, Shāngnàhéxiū and Mòtiándǐ both took Ānán as their teacher.
Mòtiándǐ had no disciples,
but Shāngnàhéxiū had one disciple
named Yōupó Júduō,
the leader of Arhat lineages in the Western lands.
At that time, Ānán recited the verse of Dharma transmission:
"Originally, there was Dharma that was transmitted;
Having transmitted it, one says there is no Dharma.
Each individually has awakened,
Having awakened, there is nothing that is not Dharma."
After the master transmitted the Dharma,
he leaped into the sky,
作十八變，
entered the Wind Wheel Heroic Samadhi,
and divided his body into four parts:
one part he offered to the Trayastrimsa Heaven,
one part he offered to the Sāgara Dragon King,
one part he offered to the King of Vaishali,
one part he offered to King Ajatashatru,
each erecting a jeweled pagoda for offerings.
Ānán entered nirvana, at a time
corresponding to the twelfth year of the tenth Zhou ruler, King Lì, the guǐsì year in this land.
Chan Master Jìng Xiū praised him, saying:
Duōwén Qìngxǐ,
loftily erected the Dharma banner.
Transmitted the Buddha's golden verses,
inherited the ancestral silver lamp.
Compassion was first,
wisdom was unparalleled.
Following Yǐn Guāng □,
the moon reflects the autumn river.
Shāngnàhéxiū.
The Third Ancestor, Venerable Shāngnàhéxiū,
also named Shāngnuòjiā,
is the name of a naturally growing, nine-branched elegant grass in Western India.
He was a person from the country of Mathura,
whose surname was Píshāduō,
his father's name was Lín Shèng,
and his mother's name was Jiāoshēyé.
Having dwelled in his mother's womb for six years, he was then born.
Soon after, he left home [to become a monk].
The clothes on his body naturally transformed into nine strips.
He obtained the Dharma of Qìngxǐ.
He extensively delivered sentient beings.
He greatly acted as a beacon of light.
Then he said:
"The Buddha prophesied
that two hundred years after my passing,
a sage will succeed me."
He then entered samādhi [meditative state],
and saw in the Zhàlì kingdom a son of a wealthy man,
named Shànyì, and whose family name was Shǒutú.
Later, he would have three sons,
the youngest of whom would leave home [to become a monk].
He will continue my lineage,
and greatly flourish my teachings.
I will use minor supernatural powers to go to that country,
not taking any disciples, but going alone.
The wealthy man paid respects and asked:
"Venerable one, you have come from afar,
what do you require?"
He replied:
"I have no companions,
I am alone.
I wish to appoint disciples and return to the Buddha's path."
The wealthy man said:
"I enjoy worldly life
"[If you] cannot become a monk,
and if you beget more sons,
[I] will give [them] to you."
The master said:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
Having spoken,
[he] then returned to his seat.
At that time, the elder soon after bore three sons.
The first two sons were unwilling to become monks.
The third son was named Yōupótà [優婆多],
and was seventeen years old.
At that time, Héxiū [和修] told his father, saying:
"The Buddha prophesied about this son, saying:
'Two hundred years after my Parinirvāṇa,
he will be the fourth teacher and convert many people.'"
The father, hearing the Buddha's prophecy,
then revered the Venerable one [Héxiū],
and allowed [Yōupótà] to become a monk.
The master then asked Jūduō [毱多], saying:
"How old are you?"
The son said:
"I am seventeen years old."
The master said:
"Are *you* seventeen years old?
Or is *your nature* seventeen years old?"
The son said:
"My nature is not seventeen years old."
The son said:
"Is it that your nature is not seventeen years old?"
Zǐ Bái 子白 asked the master, saying:
"Is the whiteness due to the heart being white?
Or is it due to the head being white?"
The master said:
"This whiteness is of the hair,
it is not of the heart or head."
Zǐ 子 said:
"The body is seventeen years old,
it is not the nature."
Within three or four years of being by the master's side,
he left home, received the precepts,
and then attained the holy fruit.
At that time, Shāngnàhéxiū 商那和修 told Jūduō 毱多, saying:
"The Tathāgata entrusted the Dharma Eye to Jiāyè 迦葉,
and so it was passed on,
even to me.
I now entrust it to you,
listen to my verse:
'Neither is it non-Dharma, nor is it non-Mind,
no Mind, also no Dharma.
When speaking of this Mind-Dharma,
this Dharma is not Mind-Dharma'
(fully as described in the *Bǎolín Zhuàn* 寶林傳)."
From the passing away of Shāngnàhéxiū 商那和修, the time
corresponds to the twenty-third year, Yǐwèi 乙未 year, of the eleventh ruler of the Jī Zhōu 姬周 Dynasty.
Chánshī Jìngxiū 淨修禪師's verse says:
The Womb Garment Venerable,
A lamp in a dark room.
Ears and eyes of humans and gods,
the sinews and bones of the Buddha's law.
Neither mind nor form,
neither diminished nor increased.
How excellent, the supreme sage!
A great *péng* bird in the sea of enlightenment.
Upagupta.
The Fourth Ancestor, Venerable Yōupó Júduō,
was a man from Zhālì.
His surname was Shǒutuó.
The Buddha foretold
that among the Chan ancestors, he would be the fourth,
transforming and delivering the multitudes,
just as I am today,
in this Bhadrakalpa, he will attain Buddhahood,
named Wúxiànghǎo Tathāgata.
He left home at seventeen,
attained enlightenment at twenty.
He traveled and transformed in all directions,
arriving at the country of Mótūluó,
where great crowds gathered.
He preached the Dharma for half a month,
and heavenly flowers rained down at times.
The earth spirit revealed its waist
to listen to the Dharma, and therefore
all attained liberation
(As described in the *Bǎolín Zhuàn* 寶林傳.)
At that time, every time the venerable Jūduō Zūnzhě 毱多尊者 converted someone,
he would cast down a counter.
The counters were four inches long.
They filled an entire stone chamber.
The chamber was sixteen feet high,
and the length and width were the same.
Later, the one who was converted was named Tídūjiā 提多迦.
He aspired to renounce the household life.
The master asked,
"Do you renounce the household life for the sake of the mind?
Or do you renounce the household life for the sake of the body?"
The young man said,
"I come to renounce the household life,
but I do not seek profit for the sake of the body or the mind."
The master said,
"If not for the sake of the body or the mind,
for whose sake do you renounce the household life?"
The young man said,
"The one who renounces the household life does so because of the absence of self;
because of the absence of self, the mind neither arises nor ceases;
since the mind neither arises nor ceases, it is constant.
Since it is constant, all Buddhas are also constant.
The mind has no form or appearance,
and its substance is also like this."
The master said,
"You will surely attain great enlightenment.
The mind will naturally become clear and bright.
According to Buddhist Dharma, he saved as many beings as the sands of the Ganges."
At that time, Duō Zūnzhě said:
"I now entrust this Dharma Eye to you,
you should spread it,
without allowing it to be cut off.
Now listen to my verse:
'The mind is originally mind,
the original mind is not a Dharma.
With Dharma, there is original mind,
without mind, there is no original Dharma.'"
Duō Zūnzhě, having entrusted the Dharma,
immediately entered Nirvana.
At that time, Tíduōjiā took the counters from the stone chamber,
piled them up and burned them.
He collected the relics,
erected a pagoda to make offerings.
The time was in this land, the thirty-first year, Gēngzǐ year, of King Píng of the thirteenth ruler of the Jī Zhōu dynasty.
Chánshī Jìngxū praised it, saying:
Yōupōjùduō,
eloquence flowing like a waterfall.
The Dharma mountain is lofty,
the Bodhi tree is verdant.
Counters filled the stone chamber,
the corpses bound, losing the Māra.
The nature is not seventeen,
enlightenment is in an instant."
Tíduōjiā,
The Fifth Ancestor, Venerable Dìduōjiā,
was a native of the country of Mójiātuó.
While he was at home,
his father dreamed of a golden sun emerging from the house,
emitting great light,
illuminating a precious mountain,
with a spring at the summit of the mountain,
initially named "Fragrant Gathering."
Because of his father's dream,
he was named Dìduōjiā,
translated as "Penetrating True Measure."
Jùduō said:
"The Tathāgata predicted of you:
'One hundred years after my Parinirvāṇa,
there will surely be a son who attains the fruit of the Path.'"
He also interpreted
his father's dream for him: "The precious mountain,
that is my body;
the emission of light,
that is your wisdom;
the emergence from the house,
that is entering the Path;
the spring at the mountain's summit,
that is the unsurpassed flavor of the Dharma."
Upon hearing Jùduō's interpretation of the dream,
Dìduōjiā was inwardly delighted and spoke a verse, saying:
Lofty and majestic seven-jeweled mountain,
constantly emanating a spring of wisdom.
Reverting to the true taste of the Dharma,
Able to deliver all those with affinity.
Venerable Jūduō responded with a verse:
"My Dharma is transmitted to you,
You shall manifest great wisdom.
A golden sun will emerge from the house,
Shining upon heaven and earth."
At that time, Tídūjiā, hearing Jūduō's verse,
Joined his palms and gazed upon his face.
Having received the Dharma transmission,
He traveled through various lands, delivering sentient beings.
(As fully described in the *Bǎolín Zhuàn*.)
At that time, Mízhējiā, the leader of eight thousand immortals,
Desired to leave home and become a monk.
Then, Tídūjiā said:
"If you wish to leave home,
Each of you should contemplate yourselves.
Without the need for a razor,
According to your thoughts,
Your hair will be purified of itself.
Out of profound reverence for the Buddha,
Robes will be born as *jiāshā* and transformed into the appearance of sandalwood."

At that time, all the immortals, each contemplating the Buddha, giving rise to reverence in their hearts, had their hair purified of itself, *jiāshā* robes grew upon their bodies, and their minds did not regress, all attaining the holy fruit. At that time, Tídūjiā said to Mízhējiā:
"The Thus Come One entrusted the Correct Dharma Eye to Kāshè,
Thus passed on in succession,
Even to me.
I now entrust this Dharma Eye to you,
Listen to my verse:
"Penetrating to the fundamental dharma-mind,
there is no law, and no non-law.
Enlightenment is the same as non-enlightenment,
with no mind to attain the law."
After the Master spoke the verse,
he transformed with the Samādhi of Fire and reduced his body to ashes.
His disciple Mízhējiā collected his relics
and built a pagoda in Mount Bāndú for offering and veneration.
The time corresponded to the year yǐchǒu, the seventh year of King Zhuāng, the fifteenth ruler of the Jī Zhōu dynasty in this land.
Chan Master Jìngxiū praised, saying:
"Master Duōjiā,
renounced the world without self.
Understanding the root and penetrating the realm,
he avoided empty flowers.
The body is not form or appearance,
the principle transcends words.
Benefiting beings everywhere,
how could he be like a gourd?"
Mízhējiā.
The Sixth Ancestor, Venerable Mízhējiā,
was a native of central India.
He received the Dharma from Tíduōjiā
(as detailed in the biography).
At that time, having obtained the Dharma, Mízhējiā
traveled and propagated the teachings.
Among the assembly was a person
named Póxūmì,
who desired to renounce the world.
At that time, Venerable Tíduōjiā said:
"When the Buddha was in the world,
he went to northern India and said to Ānán:
'Within this country,
three hundred years after my extinction,
there will be a sage who will come into the world,
surnamed Póláduò (波羅墮),
named Póxūmì (婆須密),
among all the patriarchs, he will be the seventh.'
The Buddha's prediction about you,
is not known to me,
you may become a monk, abandon your touching vessel,
and together attain the holy fruit."
Then Póxūmì (婆須密) abandoned his wine vessel,
put his palms together in reverence,
and deeply realized:
"In countless eons past, I offered a jeweled throne to the seventh Buddha,
who predicted that I
would become a Buddha in this Bhadrakalpa,
and be the seventh among the Zen patriarchs.
As the Venerable one says,
deeply understanding the past connections,
like seeing in a dream, the Venerable one is greatly compassionate,
I wish you would receive and guide me."
Then Mízhējiā (彌遮迦) ordained him
and he received the Buddhist precepts,
The task to be done is already completed,
I deeply understand this myself.
Therefore, I instructed the transmission of the Dharma and spoke this verse:
With no mind, there is nothing to be obtained.
I speak of a Dharma without a name.
If one understands that mind is not mind,
One then understands the Dharma of the mind of the mind.
The master entered into Nirvana. The time

Ancestor Mízhējiā,
Practiced the five supernatural powers of immortals.
Encountering the master's correct Dharma,
I realized my mind was biased.
Awakening to the awakening of the Tathāgata,
Mysterious, and again mysterious.

Was a native of Northern India.
Having obtained the Dharma of Mízhējiā,
He then went to propagate and transform
all sentient beings.
Arriving at the country of Jiāmóluó,
he performed great Buddhist activities.

Who asked the master, saying:

was in this land of Jī Zhōu, the 17th year, Bǐngshēn year, of King Xiāng of the 18th dynasty.

Fótuónántí (佛陀難提) heard the master's explanation of discourse and meaning,

The master accepted him,
Granted him full ordination, and he attained enlightenment.
